This was the second HTB box I’ve ever solved. To be honest, it was pretty easy but the privesc part was kinda guessy and somewhat misleading due to some version vulns being custom patched, intentionally or unintentionally.

As always, I began with an nmap. Nothing notable other than a web server.

Getting on the web server, I think there was a more elegant exploit, but all I really did was note the version then look up CVEs for FreeBPX 16.0.40.7.

I ended up finding CVE-2025-57819, which basically worked on the idea that in FreePBX’s ?ajax.php endpoint, the brand parameter can be escaped allowing for RCE. It’s pretty straightforward how it works:

$brand = $_REQUEST['brand'] ?? '';

$sql = "SELECT * FROM endpoint_models WHERE brand = '" . $brand . "'";

So basically within your request URL, you want to target ?ajax.php and include &brand=’;<payload>, where <payload> would be some sort of URL encoded reverse shell in SQL. To be honest, I tried crafting my own payload and possibly nearly succeeded, but I quickly gave up since I found one readily available that spawned me a shell for free lol

From there, getting the user flag was trivial. Sweet!

Now that I had a user shell, I wanted a quick and easy privesc through a linux kernel exploit. Luckily, this version had a ton of bugs

I ended up trying CVE-2022-25636, CVE-2024-1086 and CVE-2026-31431. To upload the exploit binaries, I actually figured out how to give myself SSH without knowing the password. Apparently, if you generate a public key on your machine and add it to the target’s authorised keys through your reverse shell, you can actually bypass the SSH login. Pretty cool!

All of that was for pretty much nothing though, since none of the kernel exploits worked. Apparently HTB hardens its kernels from “unintended exploits” or something, or at least that’s what Google’s clanker said. After that I tried the privesc CVEs the FreePBX version is known to be vulnerable to, CVE-2025-67722 and CVE-2025-1131. Neither worked either.

I got really close here when I got the idea of checking cron jobs, where I noticed fwconsole was actually a symlink to a file I can write. Sadly, my attempt at writing a flag cat script on /usr/sbin/fwconsole failed due to insufficient privileges since the job belonged to asterisk rather than root.

Then I found something about incrons. Basically, when something would be written within /var/spool/asterisk/incron, an incron was set up to trigger sysadmin_manager (some FreePBX thingy) with the filename as the argument.

I figured this would allow me to achieve arbitrary code execution if I could pass some argument to sysadmin_manager with a shell command. The way how sysadmin_manager works is it takes arguments in the form of module_hook or module.hook.param, where modules exist in /var/www/html/admin/modules/ as directories with hook files within them. I tried writing a privesc script to an existing hook and then creating a file with the hook’s name but that failed, due to what I believe is a mismatch between the hook’s hash registered in sysadmin_manager and the new one after my modification.

I figured my only option from there, if this would work at all, is to find a hook that takes a param allowing me to ACE, which I wasn’t going to spend time on digging through the modules for. After a quick Google search I figured api.fwconsole-commands would be the hook I need, which allowed for a Zlib compressed base64-encoded json array containing a command and a transaction identifier. Below’s my payload:


[“help; cp /root/root.txt /home/asterisk/root.txt; chmod 644 /home/asterisk/root.txt”, “txn”]

help goes first because api.fwconsole-commands requires a FreePBX command as the first command, but then I can cp the flag to asterisk’s home directory and chmod it to be readable through chaining. Anything works as the transaction identifier really. After Zlib compressing then base64 encoding it, I was able to get it to run as the param parameter within the filename, which got me the flag!

Not too easy because I dislike the undocumented kernel and service patching >:(
